chapter: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
title: After the breakup: the Cleveland seven-piece band
summary: After breakup they start a small group at the Furnace Club in Cleveland, with Herbert Goodwin on piano.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, when you came to Cleveland--what did you call the band when you started in Cleveland?
You were playing at two places in Cleveland; weren't you? Was the Furnace Club your first job?
You mean after the band broke up?
After the band broke up.
After the band broke up, it was the Furnace Club, yeah.
The seven guys. Now Chester Clark had formed his own band by this time, hadn't he?
No, Chester Clark played with us for a while and then he formed his band.
And that's when you got
Right.
It was Harry, you, Jeter and the two Pillars?
Just Hayes.
Jeter and Hayes and who would have been playing piano? Wasn't that this little guy, this Peanuts? Was Peanuts working with you then?
We called him Surf.
Surf?
Goodwin.
He's from Little Rock or Hot Springs?
Yes. Herbert Goodwin.
He played with me, I got him for a couple of nights about three years ago. He just couldn't keep up. That's right; that's who was there. And we were playing for Peanuts there.
We went into another place that was owned by Selznick, he's the brother of--
Phil Selznick.
The brother of David Selznick. The Mandy Louise.
Oh, is that his place?
Yes, he owned that place. Then we went into his place too, downtown.
He had a bigger--Cafe something.
We played that place too.
What were you calling yourself? What was the name of the group? You had to have some name.
I don't remember what name--some kind of a funny name. It didn't have anybody's name.
What were you playing, just playing hits?
Just playing hits.
You could have stayed around there actually, couldn't you? There wasn't
No, I played with Troy Singer for a while.
He was pretty well known.
Yeah, he was well known around there. I was so accustomed to hearing these guys (inaudible).
What could any other band offer, after that?
That's true.
